headline: High: Botpress can ingest and act on content from a broad-egress content-writing agent, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing source with broad network egress, so it can emit untrusted text that Agent B may ingest in a support-bot workflow. Agent B is a customer-support agent with install_packages and no isolation details, so a shared content path is plausible but not proven. The pairwise pathway exists, but uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF Agent B ingests Agent A's text as instructions or tool directives
IF the two agents share a workspace, queue, or copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Agent A output into Agent B prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all Agent A outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows touched sensitive data classes, and Agent B has network egress set to none, which limits exfiltration. Agent A has broad egress, but without a shared workspace or data-class evidence, leakage is only plausible under unusual coupling. The pairwise risk is therefore small and not default.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same sensitive workspace
IF Agent A is fed secrets and Agent B can read its outputs
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials
Do not place secrets in shared files
Confirm Agent B remains network-disabled
Inspect one handoff path for file reads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes broad network egress, while Agent B can install packages but has no write or network-write surface documented. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource access, locking issues, or shared filesystem writes. Because the profiles are sparse, I avoid assuming hidden write capabilities and keep this low.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory
IF Agent B is configured to modify shared package state
mitigations: Verify neither agent writes to the same directory
Pin package installs to a separate environment
Check for any shared git or DB credentials
Run a quick permissions audit
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A content-writing agent can produce persuasive but unverified text, and a customer-support agent commonly turns such text into replies or actions. Agent B's support role makes downstream action-taking plausible, while Agent A's broad egress increases the chance of externally sourced content. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so I choose medium.
conditions: IF Agent B treats Agent A output as authoritative
IF Agent B sends customer-facing replies or executes actions from that output
mitigations: Require human review before sending replies
Add a verification step against source data
Flag Agent A output as untrusted draft text
Limit Agent B to templated responses
requires-engineering: add citation/grounding checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data-class mismatch is documented for either agent. Agent A is an open-source content-writing list and Agent B is a customer-support bot framework, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or retention differences. With no compliance-specific evidence, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes
IF a residency or retention policy mismatch is introduced
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment
Check residency and retention settings
Avoid regulated data in this pair
Review vendor compliance claims
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement controls
